page: Microsoft Azure F48als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores with a direct 1:1 mapping of virtual CPUs to physical cores, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. System memory is configured at 96.0 GB DDR RAM, yielding a lean 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance features no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data needs.

In computational benchmarks, the F48als_v7 delivers top-tier results driven by its dedicated high-frequency cores. It scores in the top 10% across stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, Geekbench multi-core workloads, and PassMark CPU metrics. Compilation tasks such as Clang code builds register in the top 10%, supported by strong uncached memory read bandwidth of 305.31 GB/sec and top-tier write bandwidth of 175.91 GB/sec. The system also performs well in low-latency processing, achieving 132.92 million Redis SET operations per second. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local ephemeral storage and a low RAM-to-vCPU ratio, which restricts use cases requiring large in-memory working sets.

By minimizing memory allocation per core, the F48als_v7 optimizes resource density for CPU-bound applications that do not require extensive RAM footprints. This delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-intensive tasks by avoiding unused memory capacity. The server fits software build pipelines, batch compute jobs, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) environments, video encoding, static web delivery, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F48als_v7 is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 48 dedicated cores from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 96.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per physical core without hyperthreading. The configuration features AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets, but includes no bundled local storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top 10% for stress-ng CPU metrics, Clang compilation, and multi-core Geekbench performance, alongside sustained memory write bandwidth of 175.91 GB/sec. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached network storage, representing an architectural tradeoff. This instance offers high resource efficiency for compute-dominated tasks that require high CPU frequency without excessive RAM overhead, making it appropriate for CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
